goal: Publish one Immune-Brain-native Code Quality Guard contract that distinguishes blocking LLM correctness failures from contextual maintainability heuristics, applies concise integrity rules to internal Executor, code-review, PR-repair, and test-repair prompts plus standalone imm-pr-fix, preserves QA and Kernel authority boundaries, keeps source and packaged mirrors deterministic, and synchronizes current README and user documentation without adding hard style thresholds, a new role, runtime injection, schema changes, dependencies, or model-dependent gates.

acceptance.assertion: The canonical Code Quality Guard defines correctness invariants, contextual maintainability heuristics, and evidence-based Review decisions; applicable internal roles and standalone imm-pr-fix enforce their bounded portions, QA and unrelated roles remain excluded, style-only concerns cannot force rework, and current README/user guidance describes the shipped contract consistently.

The actual packaged prompts delivered through Loop carry the role-specific guard instructions while internal role authority, tool policies, foreground dispatch, packaged-byte identity, and stable Review Gate identifiers remain unchanged.
The Code Quality Guard reference is declared by the dist sync manifest and its packaged copy is byte-identical to the canonical docs source without introducing an undeclared packaged contract.
Canonical references, packaged references, internal role prompts, packaged role prompts, owned packaged contracts, and generated README bytes have no source/package drift after regeneration.
